newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge not worried by asbestos case.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge not worried by asbestos case.

text.p: Belgian insurance company Royale Belge SA said on Friday it did not expect to face a flood of claims for compensation from the European Commission after it lost a court case relating to an asbestos victim.
"We consider this case is not the first in a long series (of claims)," spokesman and board member Dirk Renard told Reuters.

The European Court of Justice on Thursday ordered Royale Belge and other insurance companies to pay the Commission 26 million Belgian francs plus interest in a case relating to a claim from a former European Union civil servant that he contracted cancer from asbestos used in an EU building.
Renard said Royale Belge's share of the payout amounted to around 35 percent of the total.
"It is not a precedent for other cases. It was not a medical dossier that was at issue," Renard said.
The insurers had contested the Commission's decision to compensate one former employee for lung cancer on the grounds of the procedure it followed in making the award, Renard said.
"We had the impression they were not respecting procedure written down in the agreement between us...We lost the case and accept as good citizens the decision of the court," he said.
Olivier Eben, a lawyer acting for a number of the victims, told Reuters on Thursday the European Court of Justice's decision opened the way for further compensation claims.
"There are around 64 cases that we know of, but there could be much more," Eben said.
Eben added that at least two former civil servants had died from asbestos-related diseases, and at least one family was also seeking damages.
A European Commission spokesman said only three claims were in their final stages or had been settled.

The distinctive star-shaped Berlaymont housed around 3,000 European civil servants and was the Commission's headquarters until the end of 1991 when it was evacuated following a report into the health threat posed by asbestos.
